notes:
I've put together notes on Revelation 17, but there are gaps. I ran out of searches before reaching wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com, the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org), newadvent.org, oca.org or netbible.org, so those traditions have no first-hand entries. I also found nothing on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace readings of this chapter. A few older commentaries on Bible Hub weren't labelled by author in what I saw, so I describe them as unnamed rather than guess who wrote them.

**The big question first: who is the woman?**
- **An end-times false religion (futurist):** David Guzik (Enduring Word) calls the chapter "the fall of religious Babylon". He says the harlot is a worldwide union of false religion that includes but is far bigger than Roman Catholicism. This harlot must be larger than any one branch of a religious institution. She is the embodiment of Satan's own ecumenical movement – the religion of the world system. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Walvoord (bible.org) similarly says Babylon here represents false religion. https://bible.org/seriespage/17-destruction-ecclesiastical-babylon
- **A real future city (futurist):** Precept Austin says Babylon is first and foremost a literal city that will dominate the world. It will be characterized as a harlot that prostitutes her moral values for material luxury. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-17-commentary
- **Papal Rome (Reformation, "historicist" reading):** Cornelis Venema (Ligonier) calls this the Reformation identification of the harlot Babylon in Revelation 17 with the Roman Catholic Church and the papacy. https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/interpreting-revelation William Perkins (Reformed, on Monergism) argues the woman is Rome, partly because only Rome ruled the kings of the earth in John's day. https://www.monergism.com/thethreshold/sdg/perkins/A%20Reformed%20Catholic%20-%20William%20Perkins.pdf
- **Pagan Rome, and any worldly power like it:** A Ligonier devotional says Babylon is a code for the Roman Empire, which was the chief persecutor of Christians in John's day, and can mean any power that threatens God's people. https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/babylon-rides-the-beast
- **A pattern that recurs in every age ("idealist"):** Venema says idealists see Babylon as forms of opposition to the gospel that recur throughout history. https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/interpreting-revelation

**Verse-by-verse notes**

v. 1: Guzik says her judgment is certain from the start, and the "many waters" mean she rules over many nations (see v. 15). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Ellicott notes the Old Testament picture of Babylon as the city that crushed Jerusalem; in John's day that role had passed to Rome. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Matthew Henry says "whore" here means a married woman false to her husband's bed, that is, someone who broke covenant with God. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-1.html One unnamed commentary on Bible Hub sees the figure as the degenerate portion of the Church of God. Another points to the deliberate contrast between this chapter and the Lamb's bride in 21:9. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/17-1.htm

v. 2: Ellicott: "drunk" means the nations lost their reason and self-control. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Guzik: "fornication" in the Bible is often linked to idolatry, so this religion looks attractive and spiritual but is not necessarily moral. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Adam Clarke reads it as spiritual fornication: kings and their subjects swallowing false doctrine. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/revelation-17.html

v. 3: Ellicott: this is the beast of chapter 13, and the woman draws her support from worldly power. He also contrasts her with the woman of chapter 12, who was persecuted and found safety in the wilderness. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Guzik quotes Walvoord: her riding the beast means it supports her, while she appears to control it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Precept Austin points out that John saw the chapter-12 woman in heaven but sees this one in the wilderness. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-17-commentary

v. 4: Ellicott compares her purple to the robe put on Jesus in mockery (John 19:2), and her golden cup to Jeremiah 51:7. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Guzik: her clothes signal luxury and political power, while her cup holds idolatry and impurity. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ The Gospel Coalition says her finery is similar to images of the goddess Roma, Rome's patron goddess. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/revelation/ Clarke applies the verse to the costly worship of the Latin (Roman Catholic) Church. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/revelation-17.html

v. 5: Guzik and Barclay both note that Roman prostitutes wore a headband or frontlet with their name on it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ and https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-15.html Ellicott: the word "mystery" tells us the name is symbolic, and "mother" means she is the source and pattern of all the others. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Precept Austin argues that Jerusalem can't be the "mother", because the Bible calls Jerusalem a "daughter" harlot at her worst. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-17-commentary Guzik and Chuck Smith both tie Babylonian religion to the Semiramis–Tammuz legend; Guzik presents it as resting on "history and legend". https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ and https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-5.html

v. 6: Ellicott: persecution marked pagan Rome. But wherever worldliness rules, there is the Babylon which has slain the saints. He thinks John was amazed at a woman allied with the monster. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Guzik thinks John was amazed because this was religious persecution, not pagan; he gives the burnings under Queen Mary as an example. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/

v. 7: Guzik: the angel's explanation focuses on the beast, who uses religion only as a tool. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/

v. 8: Ellicott: "was, and is not" means Christ's death and resurrection dealt worldly power its death-blow. Its revival is temporary and leads only to destruction. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm Bible Hub's study notes link the beast's "return" to the healed wound of 13:3, a copy of Christ's resurrection. https://biblehub.com/revelation/17-11.htm

v. 9: Here the traditions clearly split.
- Ellicott says the picture draws on Rome, the seven-hilled city, but verse 10 widens it into a symbol. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm
- Guzik says the Greek word means "mountains", not "hills", and that mountains often stand for governments. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/
- Catholic Answers makes the same word argument and adds that Vatican City is not built on seven hills, but only one. https://www.catholic.com/tract/hunting-the-whore-of-babylon
- Bible Odyssey (modern scholarship) takes it as a reference to Rome's famous seven hills. https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/rome/

v. 10: There are three main readings.
- **World empires:** Guzik and Ellicott take the five fallen kings as Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, Persia and Greece, with Rome as the one that "is". Guzik adds that the seventh is a revived Roman Empire, though he admits the passage is plainly difficult. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ and https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/17.htm The Bible Study New Testament starts the list with Old Babylonia instead. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ice/revelation-17.html
- **Roman emperors:** Barclay lists Augustus to Nero as the five, Vespasian as the one who is, and Titus as the one to come. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-5.html Catholic Answers says most commentators see a line of pagan emperors here. https://www.catholic.com/tract/the-whore-of-babylon Bob Utley (bible.org) accepts the emperor focus but calls the list rather arbitrary. https://bible.org/book/export/html/21460
- **Worldly power in general:** The Pulpit Commentary sees the seven as the world power across all ages. https://biblehub.com/revelation/17-10.htm

v. 11: Pulpit says the beast consists of, and is formed by the seven: Satan's worldly power summed up. https://biblehub.com/revelation/17-11.htm Guzik: the beast is the Antichrist, sharing the traits of earlier empires. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Barclay links it to the Nero-returns legend and to Domitian. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-5.html

vv. 12–13: Guzik: probably a ten-nation alliance, like the toes of Daniel 2's statue, though some take "ten" as symbolic. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/ Barclay suggests eastern (Parthian) rulers, or simply all the world powers that turn on Rome. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/17-5.html

v. 14: Bible Hub's study page calls "the Lamb will triumph" the brightest line in the chapter, a victory his followers share. https://biblehub.com/study/chapters/revelation/17.htm

v. 15: Precept Austin: the waters show her control over the whole world, not her location. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-17-commentary Clarke, following Bishop Newton, ties the wide reach to the claim to be the "Catholic" (universal) Church. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/revelation-17.html

v. 16: The readings differ widely.
- Guzik: the attack probably happens at the mid-point of the tribulation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-17/
- Clarke: the kingdoms will be reformed from popery and turn against her. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/revelation-17.html
- Barclay: Rome destroyed by her own subject nations, her lovers turning on her. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsb/revelation-17.html
- One Catholic Answers view: the woman is apostate Jerusalem and the beast is Rome, fulfilled when Rome burned Jerusalem in AD 70. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/hunt-ing-the-whore-of-babylon-part-ii
- Precept Austin says the harlot and the city of chapter 18 are one and the same, against those who see two separate destructions. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-17-commentary

v. 17: Ellicott: the kings act with one mind; the wrath of man ends up serving God's praise. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-17.html An unnamed older commentary on Bible Hub says God did this by handing the kings over to their own desires, without becoming the author of sin. It compares Joseph being sold by his brothers and the crucifixion. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/17-17.htm

v. 18: Again the identifications split.
- Pagan Rome: Ellicott. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/17-18.htm
- The pope: one older, unnamed commentary on the same page. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/17-18.htm
- Pagan Rome or apostate Jerusalem: Catholic Answers. https://www.catholic.com/tract/the-whore-of-babylon
- A system of government with no place for God: Utley says Which city is not the issue. https://bible.org/seriespage/revelation-17-18
- An evil end-times world system under the Antichrist: GotQuestions. https://www.gotquestions.org/whore-Babylon-mystery.html

**Other views**
- **Catholic:** Catholic Answers argues the woman must have existed in the first century, since she killed apostles and prophets. So she can only be pagan Rome or apostate Jerusalem, never Christian Rome. https://www.catholic.com/tract/the-whore-of-babylon It also says Luther and Calvin identified the papacy as the Antichrist and the Catholic Church as the Whore of Babylon. This is a Catholic site reporting the Reformers' view, not their own Lutheran or Reformed sources. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-time-is-near
- **Modern scholarship:** Bible Odyssey says that to John, Rome was literally the seat of all evil. https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/rome/
